Bill.BriefDescription: Restricting the use of automated license plate recognition systems.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to restricting the use of automated license platerecognition systems; amending RCW 46.63.020; adding a new section tochapter 46.64 RCW; and prescribing penalties.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 46.64 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) For purposes of this section: (a) "Automated license plate recognition system" means a system ofone or more mobile or fixed highspeed cameras combined with computeralgorithms to convert images of registration plates into computerreadable data. "Automated license plate recognition system" does notinclude an automated traffic safety camera as defined in RCW 46.63.170;and (b) "Official criminal investigation" means any observation,surveillance, assessment, inspection, inquiry, search, or other similaractivity instigated and carried out pursuant to the lawful authority ofa law enforcement agency. (2) Except as otherwise provided in subsection (3) of this section,a person may not use an automated license plate recognition system. p. 1 HB 2606 (3) Subsection (2) of this section does not apply to any state,county, or municipal law enforcement agency when conducting an officialcriminal investigation. An automated license plate recognition systemmay use only information entered by a law enforcement officer that isbased on specific and articulable facts of criminal conduct or pursuantto a court order. An authorized user of an automated license platerecognition system under this subsection may use an automated licenseplate recognition system only for the official and legitimate purposesof the user's agency. (4) Data collected or retained through the use of an automatedlicense plate recognition system in accordance with subsection (3) ofthis section are confidential and are available for use only by a lawenforcement agency in carrying out its functions or by an agencycollecting information under subsection (3) of this section for itsintended purpose and in any criminal proceeding. (5) A law enforcement agency may publish and release as publicinformation summary reports using aggregate data that do not reveal theactivities of any individual or organization and may share commercialmotor vehicle screening data with the federal motor carrier safetyadministration for regulatory compliance purposes. (6) Data collected or retained through the use of an automatedlicense plate recognition system in accordance with subsection (3) ofthis section that are not considered intelligence and investigativerecord information, or data collected for the purposes of commercialmotor vehicle screening, may not be stored for more than twentyonedays. (7) A violation of this section is a misdemeanor.
